questions.q: What frame turns SUM(TotalDue) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate ...) into a running total?
options: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
RANGE BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING
questions.explain: This frame means 'every row from the start of the result set up to and including the current row' — exactly a running total.

questions.q: What does ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW produce when used with AVG()?
options: A 7-row moving average — the current row plus the 6 rows immediately before it
A running total across the whole partition
The average of exactly 6 rows, excluding the current row
An error, because AVG() cannot use a frame
questions.explain: The current row plus 6 preceding rows is 7 rows total, and the frame slides forward with each new current row — a 7-row moving average.

questions.q: Why should ROWS be used instead of RANGE for a running total or moving average?
options: These calculations need a fixed number of physical rows; RANGE would behave unpredictably if ORDER BY values tied
RANGE cannot be used with SUM() or AVG() at all
ROWS is always faster to execute than RANGE in every case
RANGE requires PARTITION BY and ROWS does not
questions.explain: RANGE counts by logical value and would pull in extra tied rows unpredictably — ROWS counts physical positions, which is what these calculations need.

questions.q: What happens when PARTITION BY SalesPersonID is added to a running-total query?
options: The running total restarts at zero for each salesperson, instead of accumulating across the whole table
PARTITION BY has no effect on running totals
The query fails, because PARTITION BY cannot be combined with a frame clause
The running total ignores OrderDate entirely
questions.explain: PARTITION BY scopes the window per group, exactly like every other window function in this chapter — each salesperson gets their own running total.
